CONTENT PREVIEW:
Feature: Fix updateStatus to preserve original reconcile error

# GitHub Issue #186: Fix updateStatus to preserve the original reconcile error

**Category**: refactoring | **Scope**: Small

**Description**: In keystone_controller.go:139-145, when r.Status().Update() fails, the original reconcileErr is discarded and only the status update error is returned. Refactor updateStatus to use errors.Join or a multi-error pattern that preserves both the original reconcile error and the status update error, ensuring the root cause is always visible in controller logs.

**Motivation**: When a reconcile fails AND the subsequent status update also fails, the root cause of the original failure is silently lost. This makes debugging production issues significantly harder because the logs only show 'failed to update status' without any indication of what actually went wrong.

**Affected Areas**:
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller.go`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Both the original reconcile error and the status update error are returned when both fail
- [ ] Controller logs contain the root cause error, not just the status update failure
- [ ] Unit test verifies error preservation in the dual-failure case
- [ ] Single-failure cases (reconcile fails, status succeeds and vice versa) still work correctly

**Labels:** enhancement

---
Source: https://github.com/C5C3/forge/issues/186

User Stories:
- Operator sees root cause error when both reconcile and status update

<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0068): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>

    Signed-off-by: Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>
